existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: When it gives a fee estimate on a commercial or recurrent-requester request, the public body may require the requester to pay the fees in full before copying the requested documents.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Public body issues a fee estimate on a commercial or recurrent-requester request
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: provide to the requester an estimate of the time required by the public body to provide the records requested and an estimate of the fees to be charged, which the public body may require the person to pay in full before copying the requested documents
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Payment gate. Identical prepayment language appears in Section 3.2(a) for recurrent requesters; one concept cited to both.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for the first 50 pages of black-and-white, letter- or legal-sized copies requested.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 50 pages of black and white, letter or legal sized copies requested by a requester.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Fixed 50-page free threshold set by state; the city cannot lower it.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The fee for black-and-white, letter- or legal-sized copies (after the free 50) may not exceed 15 cents per page.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Copies beyond the first 50 black-and-white letter/legal pages
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The fee for black and white, letter or legal sized copies shall not exceed 15 cents per page.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling of 15 cents; the city sets the operative rate at or below it. Same concept whether a city charges a fixed 10 cents or the full 15 cents.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For copies in color or in a size other than letter/legal, a public body may not charge more than its actual cost of reproduction.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Copies in color or a non-letter/legal size
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If a public body provides copies in color or in a size other than letter or legal, the public body may not charge more than its actual cost for reproducing the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling tied to actual cost (no fixed number).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The cost for certifying a record may not exceed $1.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requester asks for a certified record
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: The cost for certifying a record shall not exceed $1.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For records provided in electronic format, a public body may charge the requester only the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Records furnished in electronic format on a recording medium
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public body may charge the requester for the actual cost of purchasing the recording medium, whether disc, diskette, tape, or other medium.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling tied to actual medium cost. Voluminous electronic requests have their own tiered caps (IL-0038).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: A public body may not charge the requester for the cost of any search for and review of the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: a public body may not charge the requester for the costs of any search for and review of the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: General prohibition on search/review charges; the only exception is the commercial-request hourly fee in Section 6(f) (IL-0035).

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Fee waiver in the public interest
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Documents must be furnished without charge or at reduced charge, as determined by the public body, if the requester states a specific purpose and the waiver is in the public interest (principally to disseminate information on public health/safety/welfare or legal rights, not for personal/commercial benefit).
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requester states a specific purpose and asserts the waiver is in the public interest
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Documents shall be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge, as determined by the public body, if the person requesting the documents states the specific purpose for the request and indicates that a waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest. Waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest if the principal purpose of the request is to access and disseminate information regarding the health, safety and welfare or the legal rights of the general public and is not for the principal purpose of personal or commercial benefit.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Soft public-interest standard the engine applies (a discretionary waiver path), so config_home structural. The public-interest test is one of the two allowed purpose inquiries (see IL-0002).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For a commercial request, a public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel searching for, retrieving, or examining the record for necessary redactions.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Request is for a commercial purpose
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: A public body may charge up to $10 for each hour spent by personnel in searching for and retrieving a requested record or examining the record for necessary redactions.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Ceiling of $10/hour; applies only to commercial requests. This is the sole exception to the no-search-fee rule (IL-0032).

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: No fee may be charged for the first 8 hours spent by personnel searching for or retrieving a requested record on a commercial request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Commercial request incurring personnel search/retrieval time
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: No fees shall be charged for the first 8 hours spent by personnel in searching for or retrieving a requested record.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Fixed 8-hour free floor before the IL-0035 hourly fee applies. Applies only to commercial requests.

existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For a voluminous request for electronic records, a public body may charge tiered caps by data size: for non-PDF data up to $20 (<=2 MB), $40 (2-4 MB), or $100 (>4 MB); for PDF data up to $20 (<=80 MB), $40 (80-160 MB), or $100 (>160 MB).
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: If a voluminous request is for electronic records and those records are not in a portable document format (PDF), the public body may charge up to $20 for not more than 2 megabytes of data, up to $40 for more than 2 but not more than 4 megabytes of data, and up to $100 for more than 4 megabytes of data. [For PDF:] up to $20 for not more than 80 megabytes of data, up to $40 for more than 80 megabytes but not more than 160 megabytes of data, and up to $100 for more than 160 megabytes of data.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: One concept (voluminous electronic-data cap) with two format bases (PDF vs non-PDF) kept in one row per the do-not-split guidance. All tiers are ceilings.
